name: Python
reason: Primary language across data science, AI engineering, automation, and backend APIs.
evidence: Requested across data, ML, AI, cloud, and backend engineering vacancies.

name: SQL
reason: Foundational querying language for analytics, business intelligence, and relational backends.
evidence: Core requirement in analyst, data scientist, and full-stack roles.

name: Excel
reason: Remains ubiquitous for financial modelling and rapid ad-hoc business reporting.
evidence: Frequently paired with SQL and Power BI in analyst roles.

name: Power BI
reason: Widely adopted enterprise BI platform for interactive KPI dashboards and DAX modelling.
evidence: High demand across business and data analyst openings.

name: Data Visualization
reason: Essential for communicating analytical findings clearly to stakeholders.
evidence: Appears alongside Power BI, Tableau, and Matplotlib.

name: Machine Learning
reason: Core capability for predictive modelling, recommendation systems, and risk scoring.
evidence: Mandatory for ML Engineer and Data Scientist roles.

name: Statistics
reason: Underpins A/B testing, inference, and reliable model evaluation.
evidence: Timeless foundation; not outdated despite age.

name: Generative AI
reason: Rapidly growing adoption of LLM integration, RAG pipelines, and agentic workflows.
evidence: Increasingly listed as preferred or mandatory in AI Engineer roles (2025-2026).

name: LangGraph
reason: Stateful multi-agent orchestration for deterministic and LLM-backed workflows.
evidence: Emerging requirement for production agentic AI systems.

name: FastAPI
reason: Modern async Python web framework with automatic OpenAPI validation.
evidence: Preferred for Python microservices and AI model serving.

name: JavaScript
reason: Standard language for interactive web applications.
evidence: Core requirement for Full Stack Developer vacancies.

name: TypeScript
reason: Strongly typed JavaScript improving maintainability in production React/Node apps.
evidence: Increasingly replacing plain JS in modern frontend teams.

name: React
reason: Dominant component-based UI library for modern web applications.
evidence: Most frequently requested frontend framework in full-stack openings.

name: Node.js
reason: Widely used JavaScript runtime for APIs and real-time services.
evidence: Consistent demand in full-stack stacks.

name: Docker
reason: Standard containerization for reproducible local and cloud deployments.
evidence: Requested across backend, cloud, and ML deployment roles.

name: Cloud Computing
reason: Core infrastructure skill across AWS, GCP, and Azure workloads.
evidence: Essential for Cloud Engineer and modern backend roles.

name: Linux
reason: Operating system foundation for servers, containers, and security operations.
evidence: Enduring foundational skill; remains critical.

name: Cybersecurity
reason: Growing priority around OWASP, network defense, IAM, and incident response.
evidence: Strong demand for SOC analysts and application security engineers.

name: Git
reason: Universal version control and collaborative workflow tool.
evidence: Baseline expectation across all software and data roles.

name: Tableau
reason: Established enterprise BI tool alongside Power BI.
evidence: Steady demand in analytics teams.

name: Python 2
issue: Python 2 reached End-of-Life in January 2020 and receives no security patches.
recommendation: Migrate to Python 3.11+ with type hints, asyncio, and modern packaging.
evidence: PSF EOL notice (2020) and zero modern employer support.

name: jQuery
issue: Direct DOM manipulation via jQuery is largely superseded by React, TypeScript, and native Fetch/DOM APIs in new greenfield apps.
recommendation: Learn React + TypeScript while keeping basic DOM knowledge for maintaining legacy apps.
evidence: Modern full-stack openings overwhelmingly specify React/Angular/Vue.

name: Flash / ActionScript
issue: Adobe Flash Player was discontinued in December 2020 and blocked in all modern browsers.
recommendation: Use HTML5 Canvas, SVG, and modern JavaScript/TypeScript.
evidence: Browser and vendor EOL (2020).

name: SOAP-only APIs
issue: New microservices and web apps favour REST/JSON or GraphQL over XML-heavy SOAP except in legacy banking/ERP integration.
recommendation: Master REST API design (OpenAPI/JSON) and HTTP security.
evidence: Low representation in entry-level developer openings.
